newsitem.title: INDIA: Pressure to resign mounts on India PM's party head.
newsitem.headline: Pressure to resign mounts on India PM's party head.

text.p: Pressure mounted on the leader of Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's party to resign on Wednesday after a court rejected his plea for protection against arrest in a $280 million scandal.
A court in the northern city of Patna dismissed an appeal for anticipatory bail by Laloo Prasad Yadav, who is the president of Gujral's Janata Dal party and the chief minister of Bihar state.
India's federal police have indicted Yadav and 55 others in the $280 million corruption scandal over animal welfare funds.
The court's decision paves the way for his arrest in connection with the scandal but it was not clear when, if at all, he would be held.
Thousands of paramilitary troops marched through the streets of Patna, the state capital, as a precaution against political violence, which is common in the poor Indian province.
"A red alert has been sounded all over the state apprehending violence as a fallout of the prevailing political crisis," director-general of police S.K. Saxena told Reuters.
"We are prepared to meet any eventuality."
Yadav has said he is innocent and resolutely refused to quit either post despite repeated calls for his resignation from other parties in the ruling United Front coalition.
The Janata Dal is the largest group in the fractious 15-party centre-left alliance, which took power two months ago.
A senior Janata Dal leader told Reuters that Gujral himself had indirectly suggested that Yadav resign.

"No prime minister can force any state government to do this or that. It was his (Gujral's) duty to hint at the resignation and that he has done," said the deputy, who asked not to be identified. "Now it is up to the chief minister to abide by that or not."

One of Gujral's junior ministers who had been accused in scandal resigned last week at the prime minister's insistence. The case has rocked his government, stoked tension within the alliance and embarrassed Gujral, who is regarded as impeccably honest.

Newspapers quoted coalition leaders as saying Gujral was considering dismissing Yadav and imposing direct federal rule over Bihar -- a move opposed by the alliance's Marxist members and endorsed by the main opposition Bharatiya Janata Party.
The Janata Dal leader said: "The government is watching the situation. Tomorrow if the situation comes to such a stage that he resigns or is forced to resign, the centre should be prepared for that."
